redaction.policy: Third-party identity withheld pending consent, following the convention used throughout this collection. Correspondents at the institutions are identified by role only; their given names, surnames and mailboxes are replaced. Institutional email domains are deliberately retained - anseladams.com, sfmoma.org and sothebys.com carry the fact of who was approached, which is the point of these records - while the domain of a small private photographic-services business is withheld with its proprietor's name. The studio principal's telephone numbers and postal addresses are withheld; that post was being received by general delivery in Eugene in March 2009 is preserved, because it bears on the record, while the postcode is not. The final octet of each X-Originating-IP value is withheld.
redaction.preserved: Every header bearing on date, provenance and threading is otherwise untouched: the Date headers with their original local offsets, the presence or absence of Message-ID and of Exchange organisation headers, the MIME boundary forms, the X-Originating-IP header itself and its first three octets, and in particular the In-Reply-To and References chains, whose identifiers were written by the receiving institution's own mail server and are the strongest corroboration in this collection. Message bodies are complete and unaltered apart from the replacements listed, including the sign-offs and the period Windows Live Hotmail footers.
replacements: each correspondent's given name and surname -> [name withheld]
each mailbox local part -> [address withheld], institutional domains retained
postal addresses -> [postal address withheld]; the Eugene postcode -> [postcode withheld]
final octet of each X-Originating-IP -> [final octet withheld]
a third party's personal aside inside a quoted reply -> [personal aside withheld]
attachment payloads -> removed, with filename, media type, byte count and SHA-256 retained

label: Preservation capture: the approach to the Ansel Adams organisation (8-9 August 2008)
note: Two outbound messages of 2008-08-08 Pacific time, about twenty minutes apart, to a named representative at anseladams.com. One carries San Francisco.zip; the other carries eight of its eleven frames loose. These are the earliest documents held in this collection. The two differ in provenance and should not be treated alike: see headerProvenance.

items.subject: Ansel Adams Visits SanFrancisco
items.note: The archive message. Retains original Hotmail headers and is the better-evidenced of the two.

original.note: Held by the studio on separate media; exported from its own mailbox 2026-09-20. The checksum is published so the held file can be shown to be unaltered without its contents being disclosed. It can be released, in whole or in part, if the third party consents or on request from the institution addressed.

items.subject: Ansel Adams San Francisco
items.note: The loose-photographs message. Its headers were rewritten by Exchange Online, a platform that did not exist in 2008, so its Date does not independently authenticate itself.

headerProvenance.assessment: One of these two files passed through a later platform that rewrote its headers; the other did not. Of the nine messages captured across this collection, this is the only one affected.
corroboration: The attached archive is byte-identical to San Francisco.zip, whose SHA-256 is published in evidence-sothebys-approach-2008 as the attachment sent to the auction house on 2008-08-14.
The eight loose photographs are byte-identical to eight members of that same archive.
EXIF DateTimeOriginal across the archive runs 2008-08-08 00:05:33 to 00:10:22.
EXIF camera model is FUJIFILM FinePix1300, agreeing with both messages' description of a 1.3 megapixel camera.
The museum letter of 2008-08-11 names the recipient of these two messages as a contact at an Adams institution, so an independently held document attests this approach.

ordering.byHeaders: The photographs message is stamped about twenty minutes before the archive one.
ordering.byText: The archive message reads as a first delivery; the photographs message gives a telephone number 'again' and sends frames loose rather than archived.
ordering.complication: The two give telephone numbers differing in a single digit, so one contains a typing error and neither orders them.
ordering.conclusion: Not established. Nothing in this collection depends on it.

negativeFinding.scope: The receiving organisation has not been approached about either message and no reply to either is held. Absence of a reply in the studio's mailbox is not evidence that none was sent.
